name: get-env

Values of credential-like names (a KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL, AUTH or COOKIE name segment) are masked as "<redacted>" unless GET_ENV_INCLUDE_SECRETS is set to 1 or true in the server's environment.

repeat.description: How many times to repeat the region in the result (1-3)

name: gzip-file-as-resource
description: Compresses a single file using gzip compression. Depending upon the selected output type, returns either the compressed data as a gzipped resource or a resource link, allowing it to be downloaded in a subsequent request: during the current session for a 2025-era client, or for ten minutes at a minted URI on protocol version 2026-07-28.

name.description: Name of the output file (at most 255 characters)

data.description: URL or data URI of the file content to compress

outputType.description: How the resulting gzipped file should be returned. 'resourceLink' returns a link to a resource that can be read later, 'resource' returns a full resource object.

name: trigger-list-changed
description: Sends a notifications/<list>/list_changed for the tool, prompt or resource list. On protocol version 2026-07-28 it is delivered on each subscriptions/listen stream that asked for that list; a 2025-era client receives it unsolicited.

list.description: Which list to announce as changed

name: trigger-log-messages
description: Sends one log message at each logging level during the call. On protocol version 2026-07-28 only the messages at or above the level the request names in _meta (io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel) are sent, and none if it names no level; a 2025-era client gets those at or above the level it set with logging/setLevel. Deprecated: logging is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28.

name: trigger-long-running-operation
description: Demonstrates a long running operation with progress updates.

duration.description: Duration of the operation in seconds

steps.description: Number of steps in the operation

name: trigger-resource-update
description: Sends a notifications/resources/updated for a resource URI. On protocol version 2026-07-28 it is delivered on each subscriptions/listen stream whose resourceSubscriptions name the URI; a 2025-era client receives it once it has called resources/subscribe for the URI.

uri.description: The URI of the resource to announce as updated, e.g. demo://resource/dynamic/text/1

name: toggle-simulated-logging
description: Toggles simulated, random-leveled logging on or off. Deprecated: 2025-era clients only, since protocol version 2026-07-28 removes logging/setLevel; use trigger-log-messages with a per-request log level instead.

name: toggle-subscriber-updates
description: Toggles simulated resource subscription updates on or off. Deprecated: 2025-era clients only, since protocol version 2026-07-28 removes resources/subscribe; use trigger-resource-update with a subscriptions/listen stream instead.

name: read_file
description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

path.description: The file to read as text. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

name: read_text_file
description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file to read as text. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

name: read_media_file
description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The image, audio or other file to read as base64. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

name: read_multiple_files
description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

name: write_file
description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file to create, or to overwrite if it exists; its parent directory must exist. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

content.description: The complete text the file will contain, replacing any it had

name: append_file
description: Append text to the end of a file, creating the file if it does not exist. The existing content is never changed or replaced. The text is appended exactly as given, with no newline added before or after it, so end it with a newline if the next append should start on a new line. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file to append to; it is created if it does not exist. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

content.description: Text to append, exactly as given. No newline is added: end it with \n if the next append should start on a new line.

name: edit_file
description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Edits apply in order, each to the result of the ones before it, and each replaces the first match of its oldText with newText. oldText must match the file's text exactly, except that line endings (LF or CRLF) never matter and, when there is no exact match, a run of whole lines matches if each line is equal once leading and trailing whitespace is ignored (newText then takes the file's indentation). Whitespace inside a line must match. If any edit has no match, nothing is written and the error shows the closest lines of the file, numbered, to copy oldText from. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The text file to edit. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

edits.description: The replacements to make, applied in order, each to the result of the ones before it. If any one has no match, none is written.

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

name: create_directory
description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to create, with any missing parents; an existing directory is left as is. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

name: list_directory
description: List the files and directories directly inside a path, each marked [FILE] or [DIR]. Use it to see what a directory contains; when you also need each entry's size or want entries sorted by size, use list_directory_with_sizes instead, and for a recursive view use directory_tree. Returns one line per entry. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to list. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

name: list_directory_with_sizes
description: List the files and directories directly inside a path with each file's size, marked [FILE] or [DIR], sorted by name or by size, largest first (sortBy). Use it when sizes matter, such as finding the largest files; for names only, use list_directory, which returns less text. Returns one line per entry, followed by the totals. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to list. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

sortBy.description: Sort entries by name or size

name: directory_tree
description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty), except at the last level when 'depth' limits the tree: those directories are not read and have no children array. The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory at the root of the tree. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns for entries to leave out, with their contents, matched against each entry's path relative to path. A pattern with no '*' matches that name at any depth ('node_modules' leaves out every node_modules directory); a pattern with '*' is a glob matched as written, and one ending in '/**' also leaves out the directory it names.

depth.description: How many levels to descend: 1 lists only the entries directly in path. Directories at the last level have no children array. Omit for the whole tree.

name: move_file
description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

source.description: The file or directory to move or rename. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

destination.description: Its new path, including the name; nothing may exist there yet. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

name: copy_file
description: Copy a file to a new location, without reading its content into the conversation. Copies one regular file, keeping its permissions and modification time; directories are not copied. If the destination exists, the operation will fail: it never overwrites. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

destination.description: Where to create the copy; nothing may exist there yet

name: search_files
description: Find files and directories by NAME, not by content: this tool never reads or searches inside files. It walks the tree under 'path' and matches a glob pattern against each entry's path relative to 'path' (case-sensitive). Use '*.ext' to match entries directly under 'path', and '**/*.ext' or '**/name' to match at any depth. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

path.description: The directory to search under. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

pattern.description: Glob matched against each entry's path relative to path, never its content: '*.ts' matches directly under path, '**/*.ts' at any depth.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns for entries to leave out, with their contents, matched against each entry's path relative to path. A pattern with no '*' matches that name at any depth ('node_modules' leaves out every node_modules directory); a pattern with '*' is a glob matched as written, and one ending in '/**' also leaves out the directory it names.

This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file or directory to describe. Absolute, or relative to an allowed directory; it must resolve inside the allowed directories.

name: list_allowed_directories
description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

name: create_entities
description: Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph. An entity whose name already exists, or repeats an earlier entity in the same call, is skipped and its observations are not added; the result lists the skipped names in `skipped`. Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

entities.description: The entities to create, each with a name unique in the graph

name: create_relations
description: Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: The relations to create. Both ends must name existing entities; a relation already in the graph is not added again

name: add_observations
description: Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity to add the observations to

contents.description: An array of observation contents to add

observations.description: The observations to add, grouped by entity. Each entity must already exist; an observation it already has is not added again

name: delete_entities
description: Delete whole entities from the knowledge graph, together with every relation that points to or from them and all their observations. Use it only to remove an entity entirely; to remove a link between two entities and keep both, use delete_relations, and to remove facts from an entity, use delete_observations. Cannot be undone.

entityNames.description: An array of entity names to delete

name: delete_observations
description: Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity containing the observations

observations.description: An array of observations to delete

deletions.description: The observations to delete, grouped by entity, each matched by its exact text

name: delete_relations
description: Delete specific relations (from, to, relationType) from the knowledge graph and keep the entities they connect. Each relation must match an existing one exactly on all three fields; if unsure, call open_nodes (or search_nodes) first to read the stored relationType. Use it to remove a link between two entities; to remove an entity itself, use delete_entities. Cannot be undone.

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: An array of relations to delete

name: read_graph
description: Read the entire knowledge graph: every entity with its observations, and every relation. The result grows with the graph, so use this only when you need everything; prefer search_nodes to find entities by keyword and open_nodes to read entities whose names you know.

entityTypes.description: Return only entities whose entityType is one of these (exact match), and only the relations that touch one of them. Omit to return every entity.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name: search_nodes
description: Search the knowledge graph for entities whose name, type or observations contain the query (case-insensitive). Use this when you have a keyword, a topic or part of a name but not the exact entity names. Prefer open_nodes when you already know the exact names, and use read_graph only when you need the whole graph. Returns the matching entities and every relation that touches one of them.

query.description: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

limit.description: Return at most this many matching entities (the first matches, in stored order), with the relations that touch them. Omit to return every match.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name: open_nodes
description: Retrieve specific entities by their exact names, with every relation that touches one of them. Use this when you already know the names (from the conversation, or from an earlier search_nodes or read_graph result); it is the cheapest way to read entities you can name. Prefer search_nodes when you only have a keyword or part of a name. Names that do not exist are skipped.

names.description: An array of entity names to retrieve

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name: sequentialthinking
description:
A detailed tool for dynamic and reflective problem-solving through thoughts.
Each thought can build on, question, or revise previous insights as understanding deepens.

When to use this tool:
- Breaking down complex problems into steps
- Planning and design with room for revision
- Analysis that might need course correction
- Problems where the full scope might not be clear initially
- Tasks that need to maintain context over multiple steps
- Situations where irrelevant information needs to be filtered out

You should:
1. Estimate totalThoughts up front and adjust it up or down as you go; thoughtNumber may exceed it
2. Question or revise earlier thoughts (isRevision with revisesThought), or branch (branchFromThought with branchId)
3. Express uncertainty, and ignore information irrelevant to the current step
4. Generate a solution hypothesis, verify it against the earlier steps, and repeat until satisfied
5. Set nextThoughtNeeded to false only when truly done and a satisfactory answer is reached

nextThoughtNeeded.description: Whether another thought step is needed

totalThoughts.description: Estimated total thoughts needed (numeric value, e.g., 5, 10)
